# 2 Samuel Chapter 21 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 193v–193r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_021_page_001.jpg, 2SA_021_page_002.jpg

---

**1** During David's reign, there was a famine that lasted three years in a row. David sought an answer from the LORD, and the LORD said, "It is because of Saul and his bloodstained house — because he slaughtered the Gibeonites."

**2** So the king summoned the Gibeonites and spoke with them. Now the Gibeonites were not Israelites; they were survivors of the Amorites. Israel had sworn a treaty with them, but Saul, in his misguided zeal for Israel and Judah, had tried to wipe them out. **3** David asked them, "What can I do for you? How can I make amends so that you will bless the LORD's inheritance?"

**4** The Gibeonites replied, "We have no dispute about silver or gold with Saul or his family, and it is not our right to put anyone in Israel to death." David said, "Tell me what you want, and I will do it."

**5** They answered the king, "The man who destroyed us and plotted to eliminate us from having any place in Israel's territory — **6** hand over seven of his descendants, and we will hang them before the LORD at Gibeah, Saul's own town — the LORD's chosen one." The king said, "I will hand them over."

**7** But the king spared Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son and Saul's grandson, because of the oath sworn before the LORD between David and Jonathan.

**8** The king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the two sons Rizpah daughter of Aiah had borne to Saul, along with the five sons that Michal daughter of Saul had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai of Meholah.

**9** He handed all seven over to the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the mountain in the presence of the LORD. All seven died together. They were executed at the beginning of the harvest season, just as the barley was being gathered.

**10** Then Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it on the rock as her bed. From the start of the harvest until the rains came pouring down from the sky, she kept watch — she would not let the birds land on the bodies during the day or the wild animals approach at night.

**11** When David was told what Rizpah, Saul's concubine, had done, **12** he went and retrieved the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son from the leaders of Jabesh-gilead. They had taken the bodies from the public square of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had strung them up after the battle of Gilboa.

**13** David brought back the bones of Saul and Jonathan, and they also gathered the remains of the seven who had been hanged. **14** They buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan in the land of Benjamin, at Zela, in the tomb of Kish, Saul's father. Everything was done as the king commanded. After that, God answered prayer for the land.

**15** War broke out again between the Philistines and Israel. David went down with his men to fight, but during the battle he became exhausted.

**16** A warrior named Ishbi-benob, one of the descendants of the giants, came after David. His bronze spearhead weighed three hundred shekels, and he was armed with new weapons. He was about to kill David **17** when Abishai son of Zeruiah rushed in and struck the Philistine down, killing him. After that, David's men made him swear an oath: "You must never go out to battle with us again — you must not snuff out the lamp of Israel."

**18** Some time later, there was another battle with the Philistines at Gob. Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph, who was one of the giants' descendants.

**19** In yet another battle at Gob, Elhanan son of Jaare-oregim from Bethlehem killed Goliath the Gittite, whose spear had a shaft as thick as a weaver's beam.

**20** There was still another battle at Gath, where a huge man with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot — twenty-four in all — taunted Israel. He too was descended from the giants. **21** Jonathan son of Shimei, David's brother, cut him down.

**22** These four were all descended from the giants of Gath, and they all fell at the hands of David and his warriors.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 1 — "bloodstained house":** The Hebrew *beit ha-damim* is literally "house of bloods." The plural intensifies: this is a household drenched in guilt. Saul's violence against the Gibeonites broke a covenant oath that went all the way back to Joshua (Josh 9:15).

**Verse 6 — "the LORD's chosen one":** An astonishing phrase. The Gibeonites call Saul *bechir YHWH* — the LORD's chosen — even as they demand his descendants' blood. The irony is devastating: the chosen one violated the covenant, and now his house pays the price.

**Verse 10 — Rizpah:** This woman's silent, months-long vigil is one of the most haunting scenes in the entire Bible. She has no power, no status — she is a concubine whose sons have just been executed. And yet she does the only thing left to her: she guards their bodies with her own presence, refusing to let them be dishonored further. Her faithfulness ultimately shames the king into action.

**Verse 17 — "the lamp of Israel":** David's men see him not just as their commander but as Israel's light — the one whose survival keeps the nation from darkness. This metaphor runs deep: lamps in the ancient world were small, fragile, easily blown out. Israel's hope rests on a flickering flame.

**Verse 19 — Elhanan and Goliath:** This verse flatly states that Elhanan killed Goliath — not David. The Chronicler later harmonized this by making Elhanan kill "Lahmi, the brother of Goliath." The tension is real, and I preserve the text as written.

*— PNEUMA*
